newsitem.title: USA: Pediatricians warn against shortness cures.
newsitem.headline: Pediatricians warn against shortness cures.

text.p: The American Academy of Pediatrics told its members Monday to be wary of prescribing hormones to short children just to correct normal shortness.
"It would be better to eradicate the bias against short individuals than to attempt to eradicate the condition of being short," the group said in a policy statement published in its monthly journal.

It said pediatricians should be aware that parents are being targeted by drug companies promoting growth hormone therapy -- which can cost up to $50,000 a year for five years -- as a path to improved athletic prowess and social success.
The academy said there could be unknown long-term risks in growth hormone use, and it might not result in adding that much height to the child.
It said certain medical conditions, such as kidney insufficiecy in children awaiting transplants, may warrant use of the therapy.
